title: From Permutation Symmetry to Communication Bounds and Additivity
authors: Zahra Baghali Khanian, Debbie Leung, Graeme Smith
abstract: Correlations across channel uses can improve quantum communication rates, making optimization over arbitrarily large blocks a central difficulty in determining quantum capacity. We show how full permutation invariance limits this advantage for every finite-dimensional memoryless channel. The optimized coherent information per use converges to the single-use maximum and consequently attains its supremum at a finite block length. Thus finite-block superadditivity remains possible, while the asymptotic optimization reduces to a single channel use. We also establish a strong converse for pure-source entanglement generation with permutation-invariant inputs: at any fixed rate above the single-use coherent-information maximum, the fidelity tends to zero. Beyond these communication bounds, we identify a common structure underlying completely bounded norms and the sandwiched Rényi channel quantities governing discrimination against a replacer and entanglement-assisted communication. De Finetti reduction and permutation covariance yield systematic alternative proofs of their known multiplicativity and additivity results within a shared variational framework. We further show that, for permutation-invariant inputs, correlations cannot sustain an asymptotic reduction in output entropy per use below the single-use minimum. This entropy limit holds for Rényi orders greater than one and for the von Neumann entropy, extending the role of symmetry from communication bounds to the control of output entropy.
summary: This work analyzes the quantum capacity of quantum channels, focusing on the role of input symmetry. It proves that when inputs are permutation-invariant, the advantage gained from using many channel uses asymptotically vanishes, reducing the problem to the single-use capacity. The paper establishes deep structural links between additivity properties for various quantum information measures.
main_problem: The paper investigates the quantum capacity of memoryless quantum channels, specifically determining whether correlations across multiple channel uses (superadditivity) provide an asymptotic advantage over single-use performance.
main_result: Under the constraint of full permutation invariance on the input state, the asymptotic quantum capacity per use converges to the single-use coherent information maximum, implying that finite-block superadditivity effects vanish in the limit.
method: The authors employ advanced quantum information theory tools, including analyzing the convergence of normalized coherent information, utilizing de Finetti reduction, and establishing common variational frameworks for various channel divergences.
model_or_system: The analysis is performed on finite-dimensional memoryless quantum channels ($N$) acting on quantum states, with a specific focus on inputs that are permutation-invariant across multiple uses.
key_observables: Quantum capacity ($Q(N)$), coherent information ($I_c$), sandwiched Rényi divergence ($eD_\alpha$), and minimum output Rényi entropy ($h_\alpha$).
important_parameters: The block length $n$, the Rényi order $\alpha > 1$, and the single-use channel capacity $Q_1(N)$.
main_assumptions: The results are strongly conditioned on the input state being fully permutation-invariant across all $n$ channel uses.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the convergence of quantum information measures (like coherent information and channel divergences) from finite blocks ($n$) to the asymptotic limit ($n 	o \infty$), showing how permutation symmetry constrains the achievable rates and establishes structural connections between additivity results.
why_interesting: It provides rigorous mathematical bounds on the fundamental limits of quantum communication, showing how symmetry constraints can simplify complex asymptotic problems, which is crucial for understanding resource theories in quantum optics and computation.
